title: Superposition and Wave-Particle Duality
learning_goal: Compare quantum superposition with wave-particle duality and explain the basic meaning of each idea.

stages.title: 1. Wave-particle duality
stages.content: Quantum objects such as photons and electrons can display wave-like behavior in some experiments and particle-like behavior in others.

stages.title: 2. Quantum superposition
stages.content: Before measurement, a quantum system can be represented as a combination of possible states. Measurement produces a definite outcome from those possibilities.

stages.title: 3. Do not confuse the ideas
stages.content: Wave-particle duality describes how quantum objects can exhibit both wave-like and particle-like properties. Superposition describes a quantum state containing multiple possible outcomes before measurement.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: An electron can form an interference pattern, showing wave-like behavior, yet arrive at a detector as a localized event, showing particle-like behavior.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A photon produces an interference pattern but is detected at one specific location. Which quantum idea does this illustrate most directly?
stages.hint: Think about showing both wave-like and particle-like behavior.
stages.alternate_explanation: Interference is a wave effect, while a single localized detection is particle-like.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, describe wave-particle duality, describe superposition in plain language, and distinguish the two concepts without claiming that measurement outcomes can be predicted with certainty.
